features.claim: Brachiosaurus had longer forelimbs than hindlimbs.

features.claim: Brachiosaurus was a very tall plant-eating dinosaur.

features.claim: Its teeth were peg-like and adapted for stripping leaves rather than chewing.

features.claim: Brachiosaurus was a quadruped with a large trunk with a high-ellipsoid cross section, a long, muscular tail and slender, columnar limbs.
features.quote: Like all sauropod dinosaurs, Brachiosaurus was a quadruped with a small skull, a long neck, a large trunk with a high-ellipsoid cross section, a long, muscular tail and slender, columnar limbs.

features.claim: The overall build of Brachiosaurus resembles a giraffe more than any other living animal.

not_this.claim: Old pictures showed sauropods using their large nasal openings as snorkels when submerged, but this was an error.
not_this.quote: Traditionally, the fleshy nostrils of sauropods were thought to have been placed likewise on top of the head, roughly at the rear of the bony nostril opening, because these animals were erroneously thought to have been amphibious, using their large nasal openings as snorkels when submerged.

not_this.claim: Most popular depictions of Brachiosaurus are in fact based on Giraffatitan, a different genus.
not_this.quote: Most popular depictions of Brachiosaurus are in fact based on Giraffatitan, a genus of brachiosaurid dinosaur from the Tendaguru Formation of Tanzania.

not_this.claim: Most full-body reconstructions of Brachiosaurus are based on the related African dinosaur Giraffatitan.

debated.claim: The neck posture of brachiosaurids is debated, with estimates ranging from near-vertical to horizontal.
debated.quote: Ongoing debate revolves around the neck posture of brachiosaurids, with estimates ranging from near-vertical to horizontal orientations.

debated.claim: The length of Brachiosaurus has been estimated at 20–22 meters and 18 meters.

debated.claim: The mass of the holotype specimen has been estimated within the range of 28.3–46.9 metric tons.
